newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria coalition ends crisis over bank sale.
newsitem.headline: Austria coalition ends crisis over bank sale.

text.p: Austria's two coalition parties on Sunday patched up a deal over the privatisation of the country's second biggest bank, apparently ending a crisis threatening the government's survival.

After 11 hours of crisis talks, Social Democrat Chancellor Franz Vranitzky and the leader of the junior coalition partner, Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schussel, said a decision on the bank sale had been decided.
"I can tell you that the state's stake in Creditanstalt will go to the highest bidder which is Bank Austria," Vranitzky told reporters.

The conservatives had opposed the sale of Creditanstalt, once bankers to the former imperial Habsburg family, to Bank Austria, which is indirectly controlled by the Social Democrat-dominated City of Vienna.

The two parties struck a deal which effectively sees the privatisation of Bank Austria with the bank guaranteeing a buyout of Creditanstalt's small shareholders -- two points which the conservatives had insisted on.

The crisis session of coalition leaders had been called for the first time since a snap general election in December 1995 in an atmosphere of mutual recrimination over the privatisation of the flagship bank.
